text:
Seth Jones has gone from punchline contract in Chicago to Stanley Cup winner to, a month into this season, the subject of Norris Trophy columns (The Rat Trick made that case on Nov. 5). He has 22 points in 21 games, 14 of them on the power play, and plays almost 25 minutes a night for the Panthers.

The points are real in the sense that nothing lucky is propping them up. Florida takes 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, three points better than without him, and his on-ice shooting is, if anything, a little cold. What has changed is his role: at more than two and a half points per 60 he's scoring at well over double a typical defenseman's rate, mostly by quarterbacking the top power play.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows both sides of him. He stops 18% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% for a typical defenseman, but only 30% of his exits keep possession. Evolving-Hockey had him a solid, not spectacular, 1.2 wins last season. The Norris talk rides on the power play staying hot.
